record.context_brief: Shifted convolution sums for cusp forms
record.original_question: Let g be a primitive cusp form of weight k for Gamma_0(N), normalized so that its first Fourier coefficient is 1 and written as g(z) = sum_{n>=0} lambda_g(n) n^((k-1)/2) e(nz). Let F(x,y) be a smooth weight function supported on (X/4, 4X] x [Y/4, 4Y], satisfying the derivative bounds stated in the paper, and define the shifted convolution sum D_g(ell_1, ell_2; h) = sum_{ell_1 m +/- ell_2 n = h} lambda_g(n) lambda_g(m) F(ell_1 m, ell_2 n) for coprime ell_1 and ell_2. Determine how the explicit constant in the known asymptotic upper bounds depends on k and N, and in the full modular-group case prove a weight-uniform asymptotic upper bound useful for Rankin-Selberg moment problems with large weights.

evidence.quote: Consider the shifted convolution sum Dg (ℓ1 , ℓ2 ; h) = sum_{ℓ1 m±ℓ2 n=h} λg (n)λg (m)F (ℓ1 m, ℓ2 n), where ℓ1 and ℓ2 are coprime.

Determine the dependence of the explicit constant on k and N. For a primitive cusp form g of weight k for the full modular group, establish an asymptotic upper bound that is uniform in the weight aspect.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $g$ be a primitive holomorphic cusp form of even integer weight $k$ for the Hecke congruence subgroup $\Gamma_0(N)$, normalized so that its first Fourier coefficient equals $1$, and write its Fourier expansion at the cusp at infinity as
$$g(z) = \sum_{n \ge 1} \lambda_g(n)\, n^{(k-1)/2}\, e(nz), \qquad e(x)=e^{2\pi i x}.$$
For real parameters $X,Y \ge 1$, let $F:(0,\infty)\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a smooth weight function supported in $(X/4, 4X]\times[Y/4,4Y]$ and satisfying the standard derivative bounds
$$x^{i} y^{j}\, \frac{\partial^{i+j} F}{\partial x^{i}\,\partial y^{j}}(x,y) \;\ll_{i,j}\; 1 \qquad (i,j\ge 0).$$
For coprime positive integers $\ell_1,\ell_2$ and a nonzero integer $h$, define the shifted convolution sum
$$D_g(\ell_1,\ell_2;h) \;=\; \sum_{\ell_1 m \pm \ell_2 n = h} \lambda_g(m)\,\lambda_g(n)\, F(\ell_1 m,\, \ell_2 n).$$
Two questions are posed:

(a) In the known asymptotic upper bounds for $D_g(\ell_1,\ell_2;h)$, determine explicitly how the implied constant depends on the weight $k$ and the level $N$.

(b) In the case $N=1$ (full modular group), establish an asymptotic upper bound for $D_g(\ell_1,\ell_2;h)$ that is uniform in the weight aspect, of a strength suitable for applications to moment problems for Rankin–Selberg $L$-functions $L(s, g\times g)$ with large weight $k$.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature contains many asymptotic estimates for shifted convolution sums of Fourier coefficients of GL(2) cusp forms (Blomer–Harcos, Holowinsky, Michel, etc.), but explicit and weight-uniform dependence on $k$ (and $N$) usable for large-weight Rankin–Selberg moment problems is not standard, and the question of obtaining such weight-uniform asymptotics for the full modular group appears to remain open. No source was found establishing the requested uniform bound in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Holowinsky's sieve bound for shifted convolution sums
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds for shifted convolution sums of Fourier coefficients of holomorphic cusp forms with explicit dependence on parameters.
status_evidence.claim: Existing bounds typically suppress or only partially track the dependence on the weight k and level N.

status_evidence.title: Shifted convolution sums and asymptotic analysis
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work obtains asymptotic formulas for shifted convolution sums of coefficients of L-functions associated with Hecke eigenforms.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research addresses asymptotics for shifted convolution sums but does not settle weight-uniform constants in the form requested.
